Long ago, in the time when Chaos came to the world, Oxyotl was one of the rarest breeds of Skink: a Chameleon who could control the colour of his scales at will. He and his band defended Mage-Lord Pocaxalan in his last-ditch effort to save the city with a great spell. But alas, the fickle powers of Chaos tricked Pocaxalan, and he tapped too deeply into the howling Winds of Magic. The Slann and his last protectors were sucked into the Realm of Chaos.\n\nNo more Chameleon Skinks spawned after the disappearance of Oxyotl. Now, somehow, he has returned from the Realm of Chaos, and the Chameleons have begun to appear again. Chameleon Skinks do not dwell within the temple-cities, but instead strike out deep into the Lustrian jungles. During invasions or times of war, they appear to put themselves at the disposal of the Skink Chiefs.
Return of the Chameleon Skinks
Once in a century, when the stars are aligned, the Spawning Pools give birth to just one Skink, gifted with the power of the Ancients. This is such a day.
The Birth of a Blessed Skink
Praissse the Creatorsss!
The deep contemplation of the Great Plan and the will of the Old Ones is soothing. Memories of a world, untainted by Chaos, can set the mind back on its straight path.
The Great Plan is soothing.
The march of ages and the power of Chaos takes a steady toll on the mind of the Slann. Only through deep contemplation and avoiding all contact with this tainted world can they protect their souls.
My mind is unravelling.

The Great Plan must be achieved.
 Your behavior is not in line with the stars, we must realign the efforts of this city-temple to the will of the gods. Acknowledge your defective actions and relinquish the leadership of this city.
 If you persist in this faulty behavior, we will be forced to assume direct control of all your assets by force.

 The Old Ones are wise in all things
I admit my faultsss...
You are defffective!

The Great Plan must be achieved.
 With your petty request for illegitimate power, you've revealed clear failings within your soul. I must therefore act to defend the interests of the Mage-Priests in their absence by subduing this menace within our midst.
 You must be submitted and corrected,
 for the glory of the Old Ones!
The realignment will occur, regardlessss!

The Great Plan must be achieved.
 I recognize the fault within my thoughts and understand my defective soul might have compromised the will of our Creators. I therefore relinquish my task unto you and submit for re-education.

 Praised be the Old Ones.
Now I will realign uss to the will of the godsss.

[From.GetTitledName] has recognized [From.GetHerHis] failings in understanding the will of the Old Ones and agreed to allow us to assume [From.GetHerHis] task to realign our efforts with the gods' will. Your valuable support in this process will be remembered by the Creators once they return to this world.\n\nPraise be the Old Ones
Praissse the Creatorsss!
[From.GetTitledName] has acknowledged [From.GetHerHis] defective thoughts and relinquished lead of this city-temple to a more competent Skink.
I sssee...

The usurpers of Tulwark are gone and the old borders are restored. The lands of the Southlands answer to the temple-city of Tlaqua once more, as the Old Ones ordained when they raised it from the jungle.
The ssstarsss are aligned again.
Lords of the Southlands
From Tlaqua to the Sudenburg coast, the kingdoms of the Southlands now bow to a single master. [Root.GetTitledName] has united the scattered realms of the southern jungles under one crown.
The Southlands are one.
An empire of the jungle? This bodes ill.
More stuff ta krump!
You've defeated the warriors of [From.GetName]. According to the old rituals, all of the prisoners caught fighting in this land are eligible to be worthy sacrifices to the Old Ones.
Pillage all! Take everything!
We will take only the sacrifices.
These are not worthy, move on.
[From.GetFirstName] has raided the province of [FromFrom.GetName], snatching many of the warriors and civilians and leaving nothing but a smoking ruin of many villages.
Monstrous savages!
[From.GetFirstName] has raided the province of [FromFrom.GetName], snatching many of the warriors and civilians and leaving nothing but a smoking ruin of many villages.
Monstrous savages!

[From.GetFirstName] has raided the province of [FromFrom.GetName]. Although most of the buildings are intact, there are only a few survivors left to tell of the many screaming prisoners dragged away by [From.GetHerHis] warriors.
Monstrous savages!

You shamed the Creators: the tribute reaped from your enemies is not sufficient to perform a proper ceremony. Your miscalculation in this war is a clear sign you acted against the perfection of the Great Plan.
The prisoners have been rounded up beneath the great temples of the Old Ones. Whom will you dedicate your sacrifice to?
Imposssible!
The Great Sssun God Chotec.
The Benevolent Protector Quetzzl.
The Myssteriousss Xholankha.
The Ravenouss Sssotek!
The Great Huntress Rigg!
Kukaili, the Great Devourer!
All the Great Old Ones!
Sacrifice some, but keep the best for my harem!
Ssserena, the Sssnake-Goddessss!
A Mage-Priest died under your care! This cannot be part of the Great Plan, your gross inefficiency in the most holy of the tasks shows your being to be defective beyond measure.
No no no no no no no!!!

A Mage-Priest died under the care of one of your appointed chiefs! This cannot be part of the Great Plan, the gross inefficiency of your helper in the most holy of the tasks shows your being also to be seriously defective.
Sssshh.. How could it be!?!

All Slann are dead! They're all dead! This is not what the Old Ones envisioned! They've left you alone, with no guidance, no signs to be interpreted! The world is doomed and all the Lizardmen with it!
SsssshhhaaaaAAAAHH!!!

The other Lizardmen do not understand your motives, they do not understand your behavior, so far it is removed from the Great Plan and the legacy of the Slann. It is common knowledge amongst the Skink that you emerged from your spawning pool somewhat defective.
Nonsssensse!
You boast about your personal accomplishments and crave for more glory at each step of the journey. Too close you associate yourself with what should be the design of the Old Ones.
I am jussst overzealouss in my tasskss..!
You keep in your place and dutifully perform your tasks. Truly, you are a productive and gregarious servant, working for the fruition of the Old Ones' Great Plan.
I belong to the Creatorsss!

You keep missing work, underperforming, trying to constantly avoid responsibility. The Creators designed the Skinks to be loyal and productive servants, to behave as irresponsibly as you do is to go against your very nature.
Jussst a minute to ressst, no?
You work tirelessly and always crave for more tasks to be completed. Truly, you are a paragon of what it means to be a Skink: productive and efficient.
I work for the Great Plan.

You are always quick to anger, ready to act violently against whatever presents to be an issue to yourself. Such a behavior could be forgivable in a Saurus, but a Skink is not made for violence and such outburst can only hint to some inherent deviance in your soul.
Well, ssscrew YOU!

You always keep a cooler blood than any of your peers and approach all your troubles with a calm and rational mind. Thus is what a Skink should be and you cannot fail to set a great example for all the younger spawns.
Good, good.
A Skink should always act and speak openly to his spawn siblings. Your honesty and clarity can only quicken the achievement of the Great Plan through coordinated effort.
Liess are uselesss in the face of the Old Onesss.
Your deceptive nature is a deviance and a frustration for all other Skinks around you. The Old Ones made you to cooperate and work together, but your deceptions make you unreliable.
It isss sstill for the greater good!

You like the glittering of gold and to keep such trinkets for yourself, but what does gold matter to the Ancients? Only lesser races, the savage mammals, should find any sort of solace by staring at a shiny useless metal.
But.. but.. it'ss sssso pretty!
You find an unhealthy joy in giving away trinkets and resources to those around you, even though the legacy of the Old Ones is neither cheap nor to be squandered.
Ssshould it be let to wassste?

You rarely know fear and gladly throw yourself in battle, this would be expected from a Saurus, but Skinks are made to be stewards and workers, not warriors. Your lack of fear might cloud your judgement and cause you to rush to a miscalculated action.
Doess it matter, if I win?
You trust in the Old Ones and spend all your waking thoughts on how to better serve them and quicken the achievement of the Great Plan. All Skinks look up to you as a paragon of zealotry.
The Old Ones are with us.

Your lack of faith in the design of the Old Ones is abhorrent. Nothing should be more important than understanding and achieving the Great Plan, yet you often find yourself wasting thoughts on other frivolous matters.
There'sss more to thiss life than the Great Plan!

They're mimicking a constellation we sshould look for!
They're sshowing the flow of magic around him!
He called them to ussse ass magic component!
They're ssucking hiss sweat! Ssshoo them!!

He demands a sssacrifice be made in hiss name!
Hiss ssskin is dry! Wassh him!
He wantss to eat ssome maggot ssoup!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] stirred from his trance for a few heartbeats to make the will of the Old Ones clear: one of the ancient tablets from before the fall of the Polar Gates lies in [tablet_kingdom.GetName]. Even now the agents of the Ruinous Powers work to cloud the Mage-Priest's vision and snatch the relic away. Its recovery would be invaluable to the understanding of the Great Plan, so you are charged to lead an expedition to this foreign land and clear the way for the Skink archaeologists.
The Ancient Tablet
Mobilize our armiesss immediately!
The time isss not right. Let the tablet wait.

Foul news from afar: a great fleet of cold-blooded monsters is sailing towards [tablet_kingdom.GetName].\n The mysterious lizard people of the far west have left their jungle temples. No one can say what they seek, but it is clear their intentions are not peaceful.
The Lizardmen
We must prepare to meet them!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent out messengers in the name of [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], to inform all Skink Priests it is the will of the Mage-Priests to focus their efforts on the recovery of an ancient tablet of the Old Ones, divined into a faraway realm of savages. \n\n As a devout follower of the Old Ones, it is your duty to join the efforts of your spawn siblings.
The Ancient Tablet
Mobilize our armiesss immediately!
It might resssult in a missscalculation.

Since the start of the war, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has appeared restless in his sleep. Many Skinks agree this is a clear sign the Slann disapproves of this war and wishes it to be ended immediately.
Asss the Old Oness command!
It could be sssomething elssse...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has awoken! He has decided that victory in this war is essential to the Great Plan and will lead the realm himself until it is won.
I bow before you, Great One.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] takes your titles and leads the realm until the war is over. You wait at his court as regent and get the realm back when he sleeps again.

You have done what you could to further the Great Plan and the interests of the Old Ones in this world. Now the war is over, and it is time to return to your meditation and keep Chaos from consuming the world. You trust the Skinks to manage in your absence.
Hnnnfffhhh...
[slann_heir.GetTitledName] rules the realm again, and you return to your meditation.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not wake at the first attempt. Trying again so soon would be sacrilegious.
I missscalculated!

I will at once!

The vast majority of Lustria is covered in jungle so thick that its many levels of canopy block out the sky. Even the high peaks and plateaus are blanketed, and it is said that arboreal creatures can cross the entire continent without once stepping upon the ground. In places, the trees soar many hundreds of feet in the air and some are even older than the race of humans.
You wake drenched in sweat, your skin burning and your limbs as heavy as lead. The jungle has got into your blood, as it does sooner or later to everyone not born beneath its canopy.

[target_character.GetTitledName] has come back from the jungle shivering and burning with fever. The healers blame the foul air beneath the canopy, the swarms that rise from the swamps at dusk and the water of Lustria, which no one born outside it should drink.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetBestName] has contracted a serious disease due to exposure to the jungles of Lustria.

Great hunting cats, cannibalistic monkey-kin, and the buzzing swarms of enormous insect life makes the jungle a constant battle zone, where survival is an hourly struggle, yet most dangerous of all that hunt beneath the canopies are the giant reptiles. You have had the misfortune of stumbling upon one of the dread creatures!

Great hunting cats, cannibalistic monkey-kin and buzzing swarms of enormous insects make the jungle a constant battle zone, where survival is an hourly struggle. Yet the most dangerous of all that hunt beneath the canopy are the giant reptiles, and your hunting trips have finally led you into the path of one of them...
The beast has your scent. It crashes through the undergrowth and rears up before you, and there is nowhere left to run. It is you or it.

The jungle shifted violently in the early hours of the morning and swallowed part of [lost_village_province.GetName]. Roots and vines have torn through walls and roofs, and a whole building has vanished beneath the green. If we are not careful, more will be lost.

Keeping the dense jungle of Lustria at bay is a constant and dangerous struggle. The jungle expands with unnatural speed, and unless it is regularly cut back by burning and felling trees, it will soon overwhelm any settlement, even those of the Lizardmen - but the workers are at constant risk of being killed by animal and plant alike. Who shall fulfil this thankless duty today?
I shall do it myself.
It is the Steward's duty.
Maybe not this time.

You have spent the past months burning and cutting the jungle of [cutback_province.GetName]. It was dangerous work - the beasts of the jungle have fought back with ferocity, and the plantlife itself seems to have become more dangerous. But have you been successful?
Working in the jungle for months on end is a hazardous occupation - even when its dangerous creatures are avoided, sickness and death lurk at every corner.
Your efforts are rewarded with success: life in [cutback_province.GetName] is now a bit easier.
Your efforts have been in vain: even after months of work, the jungle of [cutback_province.GetName] will not yield to you.
[From.GetBestName] reports that the jungle in [cutback_province.GetName] has been successfully contained.
Despite my best efforts, I've been unable to bring the jungle in [cutback_province.GetName] under control.

Precious insights into the Old One's Great Plan have been preserved on the ancient plaques of the Lizardmen, but many have been lost over the millennia. However, on rare occasions they might be recovered from an ancient ruin or lost temple.

The giant reptiles of the jungle are not just a danger for civilized life, but also powerful beasts of war. The jungle is strong right now, and your subjects have managed to tame a number of the wild beasts and ready them for battle.
The jungle is dangerous, but also home to many precious things. Exotic woods and rare medicinal plants can be found there, if one knows where to search.
The jungles of Lustria are ever a danger to civilization. For reasons unknown, the creatures of the jungle have gathered into a mighty stampede, threatening to destroy all that lies in their path.
To arms! Drive the beasts back into the jungle!
[From.GetName] is overrun! For reasons no one can explain, the creatures of the jungle have gathered into a mighty stampede and are smashing their way through the lands of the realm.
Invaders have landed near [target_province.GetName]. Armed bands are cutting their way inland through the jungle, making for the temple-cities and the gold of the Old Ones.
We must deal with this at once.
Monsters from the jungle have overrun [rampage_holding.GetBaseName]. Buildings lie trampled, and the jungle is already creeping back over the ruins.
Curse this jungle!
As the rampaging beasts overcome the defenses of [Root.Location.GetName], you find yourself cornered against a wall. What remains of you is hardly enough for a burial.

The Skink scouts report a foul stench on the wind. Ratmen have crawled out of the jungle near [target_province.GetName], spreading plague and filth wherever they pass. Sotek the Serpent God hungers for their blood.

Treasure hunters have landed near [target_province.GetName]. Drawn by the tales of golden temple-cities told in the taverns of Skeggi and Sartosa, they are cutting their way inland to loot the legacy of the Old Ones.
Defend the sacred lands!
A withered Quango hatchling crawls out of the egg and stumbles towards the enemy, biting feebly at their troops to no avail.
A Quango hatchling emerges from within to charge at the enemy with vigour before succumbing and being overwhelmed by the enemy.
The heavens resound with thunder as the Quango bursts forth in full glory and casts its radiant hues upon the world. After smiting its foes, it flies off and takes no further part in the battle.

Your long search for the relics of the Old Ones almost cost you your life today, when a herd of wild Horned Ones fell upon your party among the ruins. You barely escaped with your escort of Saurus warriors.
Ambush in the Ruins
All sssacrificesss are worthy on behalf of the Old Onesss...
All sssacrificesss are worthy on behalf of the Old Onesss...

Old Ones preserve us,
 on our search, we've been caught by the wild beasts which are sacred to our progenitors, but still do not recognize our task in their mindless souls.
 My body has been temporarily incapacitated, but I shall soon retake my duties.

 The Old Ones are wise in their design
I sssee...

Old Ones preserve us,
 on our search, we've been caught by the wild beasts which are sacred to our progenitors, but still do not recognize our task in their mindless souls.
 My body has been permanently incapacitated, and I may not be able to retake my current duties.

 The Old Ones are wise in their design
I sssee...

By the will of the Old Ones, your hard search has finally given its result: you've found a fragment of one of the ancient tablets of the Creators, whose translation will allow the Lizardmen to better fulfill their ultimate task.
A Fragment is Found ( Lizardmen )
Praissse the Old Onesss!
By the will of the Old Ones, your Chief Explorer has found a fragment of one of the ancient tablets of the Creators, whose translation will allow the Lizardmen to better fulfill their ultimate task.
Praissse the Old Onesss!

It is only a question of reading correctly the right table to understand the location of the old Temple of Rejuvenation. It is an important part of the Legacy of the Ancients and must be recovered and preserved. It is undoubtedly part of the Great Plan.

Since childhood, you heard stories of the fabled philter of eternal life, gifted by the goddesses to their best huntresses. Now you have your chance to find the ancient pool and bathe into it, as the legend goes, re-emerging strong and young forever.

This will be a long and perilous voyage, but the prize will be well worth all the trouble.\n You will venture in the unknown jungles of Lustria, one of the most inhospitable places in the world, and return with the fabled philter of eternal youth.
Time to go!

You were swimming deep through one of the narrow rivers choked by the intricate flora of the jungle when you catch a series of small shadows moving the waters not too far from where you are. The savages' ambush might have been ruined, but you must fight through them to get to your destination.

You were sailing across one of the narrow rivers choked by the intricate flora of the jungle when one of your sisters is struck down by a poisonous dart. You immediately recognize it as a miyan ambush and shout to the other Amazons to shield themselves immediately.

You were sailing across one of the narrow rivers choked by the intricate flora of the Lustrian jungle, when one of your guards falls from the side of your boat, with his back covered with needles. A shrieking pack of bloated miyans emerges from the trees on both sides, starting to shoot more of the poisonous darts on your group.
Wait! We don't want trouble!
Attack!!

You hiss the order of attack to the Sauri and await in the depths of the river as the warriors emerge and maul meticulously the unwary mammals before they can react. The water has turned red and thick with blood once the Sauri swim back to you giving the all-clear.
Your arrows and spears soon find their place in the numb skulls of the miyans, killing and scaring the little men away without significant losses for your group.

Your men fire at the vile savages for some time, quickly forcing them to retreat behind the trees. You continue to shoot until you've passed the ambush point for a while, making sure the little pests are not following you.
We keep moving.

The Sauri are struck through the head by their spears and a storm of poisonous darts falls upon you.

One after the other, your Amazons fall to the poisonous darts of the miyans. Some do not even manage to take any of them before falling, an ignominious death. You are among the last, keeping on fighting until the poison takes away your last strengths.

Your men fire at the vile savages for some time, but suffer several losses and are finally overcome by the miyans. You're riddled with poisonous darts as you try to leave the boat and fall head-first into the water, slowly sinking.
Ghhhh!..

Speaking in their dialect and explaining your quest, you manage to calm down the miyans. They've dealt with Amazons before and, although it was not always a peaceful experience, they agree to let you and your sisters pass through their territory.
Hard to believe half-males would be so reasonable.

You've tried to explain you and your sisters mean no harm to the miyans and only desire to travel on, but their chief appears to have had already unpleasant experiences with other Amazons and screams to resume the attack.
Fine! You brought this on yourself!

A Saurus was leading the pack of Lizardmen on the slope of the canyon, while he was quick to action, he was also very receptive when he recognized you as a Skink Chief and carefully listened to your words before hissing to his warriors to stand down and let you pass.

You've spent years scouring the deadly jungles of Lustria, but still no trace of the fabled Fountain of Youth. Your funds for this expedition have been depleted. Perhaps it is time to abandon this foolish quest and return to your home, before dying or being driven insane by your obsession?
No! I've enough resources to fund another expedition!
I have neither money nor strength to continue.
This might finally be it. The old ruins lay before you, buried under layers upon layers of jungle plants, but the glyphs leave no doubt about it: this is the place you're looking for.
Check for traps.
Let's move!
Three of your group fall into a pit trap right as they walk on the final staircase. Luckily, you are alright.
Forward!

Three of your group fall into a spiked pit trap right as they walk on the final staircase. One of them almost drags you to the same end, but you manage to hold onto the edge and survive, albeit wounded.
Forward!
The portal to the inner temple is so close, but in your rush, you are doomed: a pitfall opens under your feet and you fall screaming alongside your warriors to a spikey death.
AaaaaAAAAHHH!!!
You were right to check for traps. There are several levers and false steps to be disabled or avoided altogether. You manage to get safely across the final staircase and cross the main portal.
Finally!

The dark hallways are covered in ancient glyphs, long eaten by damp and mould. Yet you can still make out some of the prophecies written upon them: this is where your quest will end. You know there will be a guardian, and when the Coatl glides down, wrapping its coils around the columns between you and the final chamber, and its silent warning blooms inside your mind, you are ready to bow before it.

The dark hallways are covered in ancient glyphs, long eaten by damp and mould. They are the tongue of the Ancients, which the Amazons forgot long ago. Yet you know you are close, and you feel the traps cannot have been your final test.\n Then the Coatl glides down from the ceiling on rainbow wings and wraps its coils around the columns of the main corridor to block your way. It does not speak, yet its thoughts press into your mind like a cold hand, in a tongue older than your people. You can barely understand them.

The dark hallways are covered in ancient glyphs, long eaten by damp and mould. Not that you could read them anyway.\n You are focused on the faint light at the end of the main corridor. That is your destination. You can almost hear the sound of water.\n None of your group sees the danger until the great feathered serpent glides down from above, spitting poison and fire upon you.
Guardian of the Old Ones, hear my plea!
*Try to speak in the ancient tongue*
We must attack!

The Coatl stares deep into your soul, and its voice fills your mind without a sound.\n “You were made for this task, though it is not the task you believed you were serving when you left your spawning pool. You may enter the source of renewal, so that you may serve the Creators in their final purpose. But you shall never speak of this place, nor take anything from it. Such is the will of the Ancients.”

The Coatl stares deep into your soul, and its voice fills your mind without a sound.\n “You were not made for this task, yet you are here. It is not the will of the Ancients that you drink from this pool, nor that you share its secret with your kin. You were wrong to come. Yet the Ancients still have a place for you in their design. Return whence you came, forget this place and do their true will.”
I am humbled and ready to do the will of the godsss.
This *mussst* be my task! Ssstand aside!
I recoil at your wordsss, o mighty one.

It took a messenger of the Old Ones themselves to let you understand the error of your ways, but you understand now this quest was never yours to take. You will return home, to the duties you were spawned for.
Yesss.

You try to shape the old words and reach out to the guardian. The answer comes as a storm of images and thoughts that almost knocks you to the ground. There is no doubt the Coatl is angry, and slowly its meaning becomes clear: you are not meant to be here, you have angered the gods, and unless you flee at once it will crush and swallow you.
(Lie) Let me offer myself as compensation for the offense!
Not if I kill you first!
I will do as the Ancients command.

The Coatl is surprised by your offering, but soon you feel its pleasure in your mind. You lie down, toss your spear aside, order your sisters to stand back and call to the great serpent to take its offering.\n The Coatl slithers towards you, opens its jaws and with a slow movement of its neck begins to swallow you.\n You hold your breath and wait until you are completely inside, then draw your dagger and stab the creature's head from within.
Die!
The Coatl shakes its head at the first stab, but, before you can cut deeper, drowns you in a flow of fire and poison, ending your little deception in a swift swallow.

The Coatl shakes its head, trying to spit you out, but you stab deeper, piercing its skull and cutting into his brain again and again. The body of the creature twists and whirls as your sisters start to attack it as well, until it finally crumbles into the ground and you emerge from it, covered in spit and blood.
AAAHH!!!

The great snake whirls its coils around the entire corridors, whipping and spitting and lunging with his fangs, killing a warrior with each strike.\n You strike it again and again, cutting through its scales at dozens of points, but the blades and spears can barely draw blood.\n At every burst of fire, your forces dwindle, if you do not kill the guardian soon, you will not survive.
Kill him! Kill him!
The guardian was too strong for your tired forces. With a final swoop, the Coatl burns the remaining warriors and crushes you under its deadly coils.
Arrghh.

Bleeding from a thousand cuts, the great snake finally falls, defeated. You stand over its carcass, cutting off its head and proceed further. None of your warriors survived, but that doesn't matter anymore.
I'm so close.

There it is, not like you expected, actually. It's not a fountain at all, more like a pool, shimmering with unearthly light, water boiling but exhaling no warmth you can perceive. You slowly and carefully enter, one foot at a time, bending over the surface to take a deep sip.\n The liquid has no flavor, but as it runs through your body, you feel immediately reinvigorated, you feel yourself young and strong as never before.\n The legends were true and you've been one of the very few to find the source of eternal life and partake in it!
I shall be young forever!
